metadata.name: HeliOS Coding Standard
metadata.description: DSL-like coding rules for HeliOS embedded operating system covering function structure, control flow, parameter validation, API naming conventions, scope visibility, and object validation paradigm
metadata.author: HeliOS Project

rules.name: Function Entry/Exit Macros
rules.description: All functions returning Return_t must begin with FUNCTION_ENTER and end with FUNCTION_EXIT macros. FUNCTION_ENTER declares the Return_t ret variable initialized to ReturnError. FUNCTION_EXIT returns the ret variable.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE macro.FUNCTION_ENTER AT function.start AND REQUIRE macro.FUNCTION_EXIT AT function.end

rules.rationale: Ensures consistent error handling and return value management across all kernel functions

rules.name: No Direct Return Variable Access
rules.description: Function code must not directly assign to or manipulate the 'ret' variable. Only macros (__ReturnOk__) may modify the ret variable. Direct manipulation breaks the controlled return path pattern.

dsl.rule: FORBID assignment TO variable.ret WITHIN function.body EXCEPT macro.context

rules.rationale: Centralizes return value management through macros, preventing inconsistent error handling patterns

rules.name: Single FUNCTION_ENTER and FUNCTION_EXIT
rules.description: FUNCTION_ENTER must appear exactly once at the beginning of the function body, and FUNCTION_EXIT must appear exactly once at the end of the function body. Multiple occurrences violate the single-entry/single-exit pattern.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE macro.FUNCTION_ENTER OCCURS exactly.1 AND REQUIRE macro.FUNCTION_EXIT OCCURS exactly.1

rules.rationale: Enforces strict single-entry/single-exit pattern ensuring predictable execution flow

rules.name: All Parameters Validated Upfront
rules.description: All function parameters must be validated in a single compound conditional statement immediately after FUNCTION_ENTER and local variable declarations. Validation must check all pointer parameters using __PointerIsNotNull__() and all object parameters (structures with Base_t valid field from HeliOS.h or types.h) using __ObjectIsValid__(). Numeric parameters must be validated for valid ranges before any processing occurs.

dsl.pattern: function { FUNCTION_ENTER; [locals*]; if(VALIDATE_ALL_PARAMS) { NESTED_LOGIC; } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }; FUNCTION_EXIT; }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE validation.all_parameters BEFORE any.processing AND REQUIRE validation.form == compound_if_statement AND REQUIRE pointer.validation USES __PointerIsNotNull__ AND REQUIRE object.validation USES __ObjectIsValid__

rules.rationale: Prevents processing with invalid parameters and ensures fail-fast behavior at function boundaries. Object validation provides defense-in-depth beyond null pointer checks.

rules.name: Use Pointer Validation Macros
rules.description: Pointer validation must use standardized validation macros: __PointerIsNotNull__() for non-null checks and __PointerIsNull__() for null checks. For objects with a Base_t valid field, use __ObjectIsValid__() instead of just pointer checks. Never use raw null comparisons.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE pointer.validation USES macro.validation_helpers INSTEAD OF raw_null_expressions

rules.rationale: Provides consistent, readable validation semantics and centralizes null-checking logic

rules.name: Use Flag Validation Macros
rules.description: Flag state validation must use standardized macros: __FlagIsSet__() and __FlagIsNotSet__() for checking flag states. Never use raw comparisons with zero or direct bitwise operations for flag checking in validation contexts.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE flag.validation USES macro.flag_helpers INSTEAD OF raw_flag_expressions

rules.rationale: Provides consistent flag state checking semantics and improves code readability

rules.name: No Early Returns
rules.description: Functions must not use early return statements. The only return statement allowed is the FUNCTION_EXIT macro at the function end. This enforces single-entry/single-exit pattern with controlled return paths.

dsl.rule: FORBID keyword.return WITHIN function.body AND REQUIRE ONLY macro.FUNCTION_EXIT AT function.end

rules.rationale: Ensures predictable execution flow and simplifies debugging by guaranteeing single exit point

valid: // Only exit point is FUNCTION_EXIT at end

rules.name: Nested Happy Path Pattern
rules.description: The successful execution path (happy path) must be implemented as nested if-statements, with each level of nesting representing progress through the function. Success conditions are nested deeper, creating a rightward indentation pattern for the main logic flow. __ReturnOk__() should be called in the final (deepest) if block of the happy path to indicate success.

dsl.pattern: if(condition_valid) { if(next_valid) { if(operation_ok) { __ReturnOk__(); } else { __AssertOnElse__(); } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE control_flow.success_path USES pattern.nested_if AND REQUIRE nesting.direction == rightward AND REQUIRE __ReturnOk__ IN deepest.if_block

rules.rationale: Makes the happy path visually distinct and easy to follow while keeping error handling consistent. Success indication at the deepest nesting level clearly marks successful completion.

rules.name: Else Is Bad Path with Assert
rules.description: Every else clause represents an error/failure path and must contain only the __AssertOnElse__() macro call (optionally followed by cleanup code with comments). The else clause never contains business logic or success-path code.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE every.else_clause CONTAINS macro.__AssertOnElse__ AS first_statement AND FORBID business_logic IN else_clause

rules.rationale: Makes error paths explicit and consistent, triggering assertions for debugging while allowing cleanup

rules.name: Success Return Macro Only
rules.description: To indicate function success, code must call __ReturnOk__() macro which sets ret to ReturnOK. Never manually assign ret = ReturnOK. The macro should typically be called exactly once at the deepest point of the nested if happy path, immediately before the successful completion of the function. In rare cases, __ReturnOk__() may appear in additional locations for special control flow requirements.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE success_indication USES macro.__ReturnOk__ AND FORBID direct.assignment(ret, ReturnOK) AND PREFER single.occurrence AT deepest.nesting

rules.rationale: Provides centralized success indication and allows for future instrumentation/debugging hooks. Single occurrence at deepest nesting makes success path clear and predictable.

rules.name: Error Return Via Function Exit
rules.description: Functions return error status by default since FUNCTION_ENTER initializes ret to ReturnError. Error paths should not explicitly set ret to ReturnError. Simply allow FUNCTION_EXIT to return the default error value, optionally calling __AssertOnElse__() first.

dsl.rule: FORBID explicit.assignment(ret, ReturnError) AND REQUIRE error_path USES default.ret_value

rules.rationale: Leverages fail-by-default initialization, reducing code duplication and preventing missed error cases

rules.name: No Error Return Macro or Assignment
rules.description: Never create or use a __ReturnError__() macro or manually assign ret to ReturnError. These are antipatterns that violate the fail-by-default design. Since FUNCTION_ENTER initializes ret to ReturnError, error conditions should simply fall through to FUNCTION_EXIT without modification.

dsl.rule: FORBID macro.__ReturnError__ AND FORBID assignment(ret, ReturnError)

rules.rationale: Maintains fail-by-default consistency and prevents redundant error setting that could mask control flow issues

rules.name: Cleanup on Allocation Failure
rules.description: When a memory allocation or operation fails within nested allocations, all previously allocated resources must be freed in the error path. The cleanup code must appear in the else clause after __AssertOnElse__() with a comment explaining the cleanup reason.

dsl.pattern: if(OK(allocate)) { if(OK(next_op)) { success; } else { __AssertOnElse__(); /* cleanup */ free; } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE error_path PERFORMS cleanup.free_allocations WHEN prior.allocations_exist AND REQUIRE cleanup PRECEDED_BY comment.explanation

rules.rationale: Prevents memory leaks by ensuring proper cleanup on error paths in nested allocation scenarios

rules.name: Parameter Naming Convention
rules.description: All function parameters must use trailing underscore naming convention (e.g., task_, name_, callback_). This distinguishes parameters from local variables and prevents naming conflicts with types.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE parameter.name ENDS_WITH '_' AND REQUIRE parameter.name STARTS_WITH lowercase

rules.rationale: Provides visual distinction between parameters and locals, reducing naming collision risks

valid: Return_t xTaskCreate(Task_t **task_, const Byte_t *name_, void (*callback_)(...), TaskParm_t *taskParameter_)

rules.name: Local Variable Initialization
rules.description: Local variables must be declared immediately after FUNCTION_ENTER and initialized to appropriate zero values (null for pointers, 0x0u for numeric types). All local variable declarations must be grouped together before any logic.

dsl.pattern: function { FUNCTION_ENTER; [type var = initial_value;]+; /* blank line */ logic; }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE local_vars DECLARED_AFTER macro.FUNCTION_ENTER AND REQUIRE local_vars.initialization IN {null, 0x0u, false} AND REQUIRE local_vars.grouping == consecutive

rules.rationale: Prevents use of uninitialized variables and clearly separates declarations from logic

rules.name: Use HeliOS Type Definitions
rules.description: Code must use HeliOS type definitions (Return_t, Base_t, Byte_t, Word_t, HalfWord_t, Size_t, Ticks_t, Addr_t) instead of standard C types. Use 'null' macro instead of NULL. Use 'true'/'false' instead of 1/0 for boolean values.

dsl.pattern: type_usage { USE(Return_t | Base_t | Byte_t | Word_t | Size_t | Addr_t); USE(null); USE(true | false); }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE types FROM helios.types AND FORBID types FROM {int, char, unsigned, NULL, 1, 0} IN boolean_context

rules.rationale: Ensures portability and consistent type semantics across different platforms

rules.name: Hexadecimal Integer Literal Notation
rules.description: All integer numeric literals (including zero) must be expressed in hexadecimal notation with appropriate type suffix. Use 0x0u for unsigned zero, 0x1u for unsigned one, etc. The 'u' suffix indicates unsigned type. This applies to all integer constants in the codebase, not just zero values.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE numeric.integer_literal USES format.hexadecimal AND REQUIRE format INCLUDES type_suffix

rules.rationale: Provides consistent literal notation across the codebase, makes unsigned intent explicit, and improves readability by using uniform base representation

rules.name: Internal Macro Naming Convention
rules.description: Internal/helper macros and functions must use double underscore prefix and suffix naming pattern (e.g., __MacroName__, __FunctionName__). This distinguishes internal implementation from public API which uses single prefix 'x' for syscalls.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE macro.internal.name STARTS_WITH '__' AND ENDS_WITH '__' AND REQUIRE function.internal.name STARTS_WITH '__' AND ENDS_WITH '__'

rules.rationale: Clearly separates internal implementation from public API, preventing accidental external use

rules.name: Check All Syscall Results
rules.description: All syscall results must be checked using OK() or ERROR() macros before proceeding. Syscalls returning Return_t must have their results validated within the calling context. Unchecked syscalls can lead to processing invalid data.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE syscall.result CHECKED_BY (macro.OK | macro.ERROR) BEFORE data.use

rules.rationale: Ensures errors are caught immediately and prevents cascading failures from unchecked operations

rules.name: Cleanup Code Must Be Commented
rules.description: When resource cleanup occurs in error paths, it must be preceded by a comment explaining why the cleanup is necessary and which operation failure triggered it. Comment format: '/* cleanup_action because operation_that_failed. */'

dsl.rule: REQUIRE cleanup.in_error_path PRECEDED_BY comment.explanation AND REQUIRE comment CONTAINS {cleanup_reason, failed_operation}

rules.rationale: Makes error handling logic explicit and helps maintainers understand cleanup requirements

rules.name: Check Pointers After Allocation
rules.description: After a successful allocation syscall, the returned pointer must still be explicitly validated with __PointerIsNotNull__() before use. Even if allocation returns OK, defensive programming requires pointer validation.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE pointer.allocated VALIDATED_BY __PointerIsNotNull__ BEFORE pointer.dereference

rules.rationale: Provides defense-in-depth against allocation edge cases and ensures consistent validation patterns

rules.name: Pointer-Based List Traversal
rules.description: When traversing linked lists, use while(__PointerIsNotNull__(cursor)) pattern. The cursor pointer must be validated at each iteration. Never assume list structure without validation.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE list.traversal USES pattern.while_pointer_not_null AND REQUIRE cursor.validation PER iteration

rules.rationale: Prevents null pointer dereferences and ensures safe list traversal even with corrupted structures

rules.name: Cursor Initialization Before Traversal
rules.description: Linked list traversal must use a cursor pointer variable that is initialized to the list head (e.g., list->head) immediately before entering the while loop. The cursor variable should be declared as a local variable at the function start and initialized to null, then assigned the list head before the loop.

dsl.pattern: list_traversal { Type_t *cursor = null; ...; cursor = list->head; while(__PointerIsNotNull__(cursor)) { ... } }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE cursor.declaration AS local_variable AND REQUIRE cursor.initialization TO null THEN list.head BEFORE while.loop

rules.rationale: Establishes consistent list traversal pattern with proper initialization, making code predictable and safe

invalid:
// Cursor initialized in loop header
for(Task_t *cursor = tlist->head; __PointerIsNotNull__(cursor); cursor = cursor->next) {

rules.name: Yoda Conditionals for Constants
rules.description: In equality/inequality comparisons between variables and constants, place the constant on the left side (Yoda notation). This prevents accidental assignment when == is mistyped as =.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE comparison.with_constant USES order.constant_first

rules.rationale: Prevents accidental assignment bugs that compile without warning but cause runtime errors

rules.name: Break After Success in Loops
rules.description: When searching through a list/collection and finding a match that sets the success return, immediately break from the loop. This prevents unnecessary iterations after the goal is achieved.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE search.success FOLLOWED_BY keyword.break WHEN inside.loop

rules.rationale: Optimizes performance by avoiding redundant iterations and makes search success explicit

rules.name: Blank Lines Separate Sections
rules.description: Use blank lines to separate logical sections: one blank line after FUNCTION_ENTER, one blank line between local variable declarations and logic, and no blank lines within tightly coupled logic blocks.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE blank_line AFTER macro.FUNCTION_ENTER AND AFTER variable.declarations AND BEFORE macro.FUNCTION_EXIT

rules.rationale: Improves code readability by visually separating function setup, variables, logic, and teardown

rules.name: Public API Function Naming
rules.description: All public API functions (syscalls) exposed through HeliOS.h must use the naming pattern 'x' + SubsystemName + Action. The 'x' prefix indicates a public syscall accessible to user applications. Examples: xTaskCreate, xMemAlloc, xQueueSend, xDeviceRead.

dsl.pattern: function.public { name MATCHES /^x[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/ AND declared_in HeliOS.h AND declared_in module.h }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE api.public.name STARTS_WITH 'x' AND FOLLOWED_BY PascalCase AND REQUIRE declaration IN {HeliOS.h, module.h}

rules.rationale: Provides clear distinction between public API and internal functions, making API boundaries explicit

rules.name: Internal Cross-Module Function Naming
rules.description: Internal functions exposed through module header files (*.h) for use by other kernel modules must use double underscore prefix and suffix pattern: __FunctionName__. These are NOT public API but are callable across kernel modules. These functions have kernel-wide scope and must be declared in the module header file. Examples: __RegisterDevice__, __KernelAllocateMemory__, __DeviceListFind__.

dsl.pattern: function.internal_cross_module { name MATCHES /^__[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*__$/ AND declared_in module.h AND NOT declared_in HeliOS.h }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE api.internal_public.name MATCHES pattern.__NAME__ AND REQUIRE declaration IN module.h ONLY AND FORBID declaration IN HeliOS.h

rules.rationale: Distinguishes kernel-internal API from public API while allowing necessary cross-module communication. Header declaration ensures kernel-wide visibility.

rules.name: Module-Private Function Naming
rules.description: Functions private to a single module (only used within one .c file) must be declared 'static' and use double underscore prefix and suffix pattern: static Return_t __FunctionName__(...). These functions have module-only scope, must be defined in the C source file only, and should NOT be exposed through any header file.

dsl.pattern: function.private { storage_class == static AND name MATCHES /^__[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*__$/ AND NOT declared_in any.header }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE function.module_private USES storage.static AND REQUIRE name MATCHES pattern.__NAME__ AND FORBID declaration IN any.h

rules.rationale: Limits scope to single compilation unit, preventing namespace pollution and accidental external use. Static linkage enforces module-only scope.

rules.name: Public API Declaration in HeliOS.h
rules.description: All public API functions (x-prefixed syscalls) must be declared in both HeliOS.h (the main public header) AND the corresponding module header file (e.g., task.h, device.h). The HeliOS.h declarations provide the unified public interface for user applications.

dsl.pattern: function.public { declared_in HeliOS.h AND declared_in module.h }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE api.public DECLARED_IN HeliOS.h AND DECLARED_IN corresponding.module.h

rules.rationale: Provides single unified header for users while maintaining modular organization for kernel development

invalid:
/* Only in task.h, missing from HeliOS.h */
Return_t xTaskCreate(Task_t **task_, ...);

rules.name: Internal API Declaration Scope
rules.shortName: Internal API in Module Header Only
rules.description: Internal cross-module functions (__FunctionName__ pattern) must be declared ONLY in their module header file (e.g., device.h, mem.h), never in HeliOS.h. These are kernel-internal APIs not meant for user application access.

dsl.pattern: function.internal_cross_module { declared_in module.h AND NOT declared_in HeliOS.h }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE api.internal_public DECLARED_IN module.h ONLY AND FORBID declaration IN HeliOS.h

rules.rationale: Hides kernel implementation details from user applications while allowing necessary kernel-internal communication

invalid:
/* In HeliOS.h - WRONG! Internal API exposed to users */
Return_t __RegisterDevice__(const HalfWord_t uid_, ...);

rules.name: Module-Private Functions Not Declared in Headers
rules.description: Static module-private functions must NOT be declared in any header file. They should only exist in the .c source file. Forward declarations within the .c file are acceptable and encouraged for organization.

dsl.pattern: function.private { storage_class == static AND NOT declared_in any.h AND MAY_BE forward_declared_in same.c }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE function.static NOT declared_in any.h AND ALLOW forward_declaration IN same.source_file

rules.rationale: Maintains strict encapsulation and prevents exposure of implementation details outside the module

invalid:
/* In queue.h - WRONG! Static function in header */
static Return_t __QueueDropmessage__(Queue_t *queue_);

rules.name: Subsystem Prefix Consistency
rules.description: Public API functions must use consistent subsystem prefixes: xTask* for tasks, xMem* for memory, xQueue* for queues, xDevice* for devices, xTimer* for timers, xStream* for streams, xFS* for filesystem, xSystem* for system operations. The subsystem name immediately follows the 'x' prefix.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE api.public.name MATCHES pattern.x_SUBSYSTEM_Action AND REQUIRE subsystem IN {Task, Mem, Queue, Device, Timer, Stream, FS, System, Console}

rules.rationale: Organizes API by functional area and makes function purpose immediately clear from name

rules.name: Functions Must Return Return_t
rules.description: All public API functions (x-prefixed) and internal functions (__-prefixed) must return Return_t to indicate success or failure. This applies to both cross-module and module-private functions. In rare cases, helper functions may return other types (e.g., comparison results, calculated values), but these should be exceptional and well-justified.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE function.public RETURNS Return_t AND REQUIRE function.internal RETURNS Return_t EXCEPT rare.helper_functions

rules.rationale: Ensures consistent error handling across the entire API surface and enables uniform validation with OK()/ERROR() macros

rules.name: Objects Must Have Valid Field
rules.description: All HeliOS object types (structs representing managed kernel objects like Task_t, Queue_t, Device_t, etc.) must include a Base_t valid field. This field serves as an object state marker to detect invalid, uninitialized, or freed objects.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE kernel_object.struct CONTAINS field.valid OF_TYPE Base_t

rules.rationale: Enables runtime detection of use-after-free, double-free, and uninitialized object access bugs

rules.name: Set Valid on Object Creation
rules.description: When creating/allocating a kernel object, immediately set its valid field to VALID (0xAAu) after successful allocation and before populating other fields. This marks the object as initialized and ready for use.

dsl.pattern: object_creation { if(OK(allocate(&obj))) { if(__PointerIsNotNull__(obj)) { obj->valid = VALID; /* initialize other fields */ } } }
dsl.rule: REQUIRE object.creation SETS field.valid TO constant.VALID AFTER allocation.success

rules.rationale: Establishes object validity state immediately upon creation, enabling validation in all subsequent operations

rules.name: Set Invalid Before Object Deletion
rules.description: Before freeing/deleting a kernel object, set its valid field to INVALID (0x55u). This marks the object as destroyed and helps detect use-after-free bugs if any code attempts to use the freed object.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE object.deletion SETS field.valid TO constant.INVALID BEFORE free.operation

rules.rationale: Provides defense against use-after-free by poisoning the object state before deallocation

rules.name: Use __ObjectIsValid__ for Object Validation
rules.description: When validating kernel objects, use __ObjectIsValid__(obj) instead of only __PointerIsNotNull__(obj). The __ObjectIsValid__ macro checks both that the pointer is not null AND that the object's valid field equals VALID. This provides defense-in-depth validation.

dsl.rule: REQUIRE object.validation USES macro.__ObjectIsValid__ INSTEAD_OF only.__PointerIsNotNull__

rules.rationale: Detects invalid/freed/uninitialized objects beyond simple null pointer checks, preventing subtle bugs

object_validation.description: Object state validation macros - checks both pointer and valid field

allocation_and_check.pattern: if(OK(__KernelAllocateMemory__((volatile Addr_t **)&ptr, size))) { if(__PointerIsNotNull__(ptr)) { /* use ptr */ } else { __AssertOnElse__(); } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }
allocation_and_check.description: Standard allocation pattern with double validation

object_creation.pattern: if(OK(__KernelAllocateMemory__((volatile Addr_t **)&obj, sizeof(ObjType_t)))) { if(__PointerIsNotNull__(obj)) { obj->valid = VALID; obj->field1 = value1; obj->field2 = value2; __ReturnOk__(); } else { __AssertOnElse__(); } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }
object_creation.description: Standard object creation pattern - allocate, validate pointer, set valid field, initialize other fields

object_deletion.pattern: if(__ObjectIsValid__(obj)) { /* cleanup resources */ obj->valid = INVALID; if(OK(__KernelFreeMemory__(obj))) { __ReturnOk__(); } else { __AssertOnElse__(); } } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }
object_deletion.description: Standard object deletion pattern - validate object, cleanup, mark invalid, then free

object_operation.description: Standard object operation pattern - validate object and parameters before processing

list_find.pattern: cursor = list->head; while(__PointerIsNotNull__(cursor) && (target != cursor)) { cursor = cursor->next; } if(__PointerIsNotNull__(cursor)) { /* found */ } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }

compound_validation.pattern: if(__PointerIsNotNull__(param1_) && (0x0u < param2_) && __FlagIsNotSet__(FLAG)) { /* nested happy path */ } else { __AssertOnElse__(); }

severity_levels.error: Rule violation breaks compilation, critical safety issue, or causes undefined behavior
severity_levels.warning: Rule violation may cause bugs, reduces maintainability, or violates best practices
severity_levels.style: Rule violation affects code consistency and readability but not functionality
